objectives: Recognise the kn spelling at the start of taught words.
Identify /n/ as the first spoken sound in knee, knot, and knit.
Distinguish kn words from words beginning with /k/ or /n/ alone.
Use the whole word to confirm sound and spelling.
concepts: In these taught initial kn words, k is silent.
The spelling keeps k before n even though k is not pronounced.
The vowel and ending distinguish knee, knot, and knit.

definitions.definition: A letter in a word's spelling that is not pronounced.
A letter or group of letters representing a sound.
A speech sound that can distinguish one word from another.

workedExamples.solution: The word begins with /n/; the k is silent.
Knee begins with /n/; key begins with /k/.
The first spoken sound is /n/, not /k/.

commonMistakes: Pronouncing the k in kn words.
Deleting k from the spelling because it is silent.
Guessing without listening to the first sound.
keyTakeaways: Initial k is silent in the taught kn words.
revisionPoints: k is silent in initial kn.
